info.title: Alazab Daftra work_orders
info.description: Derived from supplied API export; tenant and runtime validation required.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of work orders for the authenticated account.

Requires the `View his work orders` or `View all work orders` permission. Staff who only hold `View his work orders` see only the work orders they created or are assigned to. Workflow-type entities are excluded — only classic work orders are returned.

**Default status filter:** when no `status` filter is supplied, the list returns only **Open** work orders. Pass `status=-1` to return every status, or a specific status value to filter.

Each item is returned under a `WorkOrder` key; related records (client, staff, follow-up status) are not embedded.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by work order status. When omitted, only Open work orders are returned. Pass `-1` to return all statuses.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Open |
| 2 | Closed |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Draft |
| -1 | All statuses |

staff_id.description: ID of the staff member who created the work order. `0` indicates the account owner.

client_id.description: Identifier of the client this work order belongs to.

number.description: Work order number. Auto-generated when not supplied on creation.

status.description:
Work order status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Open |
| 2 | Closed |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Draft |

delivery_date.description: Expected delivery / finish date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be on or after the start date.

budget.description: Budget amount for this work order.

budget_currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget.

client_data.description: JSON snapshot of the client's details captured when the work order was saved.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a new work order.

Requires the `Add new work orders` permission. The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object. Only `title` is required.

Several fields are set automatically and cannot be controlled by the caller: the work order `number` is generated when omitted, `start_date` defaults to today when omitted, the creator is recorded as the authenticated user, and `status` is set to Open (or Draft when `is_draft` is sent). On success the new work order id is returned with HTTP 202.

client_id.description: Identifier of the client this work order belongs to. The client must not be suspended.

number.description: Work order number. Auto-generated when omitted; may be overridden with a unique value.

start_date.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional — defaults to today when omitted.

delivery_date.description: Expected delivery / finish date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be on or after the start date.

budget.description: Budget amount for this work order.

budget_currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget.

staff_id.description: Staff member to assign to this work order. The creator is recorded automatically as the authenticated user.

is_draft.description: Set to `1` to save the work order as a Draft with relaxed validation. Defaults to `0`.

id.description: Identifier of the newly created work order.

validation_errors.description: Field name → reason. Present when validation fails.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single work order by its identifier.

Requires permission to view the work order. Staff who only hold `View his work orders` may view a work order only if they created it or are assigned to it. The work order is returned under a `data.WorkOrder` key; related records (client, staff, follow-up status) are not embedded.

This endpoint serves classic work orders; workflow-type entities are handled separately.

staff_id.description: ID of the staff member who created the work order. `0` indicates the account owner.

client_id.description: Identifier of the client this work order belongs to.

number.description: Work order number. Auto-generated when not supplied on creation.

status.description:
Work order status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Open |
| 2 | Closed |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Draft |

delivery_date.description: Expected delivery / finish date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be on or after the start date.

budget.description: Budget amount for this work order.

budget_currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget.

client_data.description: JSON snapshot of the client's details captured when the work order was saved.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing work order.

Requires permission to edit the work order (`Edit & remove all work orders`, or `Edit & remove his work orders` for one the staff created or is assigned to). The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object; `title` and `start_date` are required.

A **Closed** work order cannot be edited and returns `400`. As with create, `status` is server-controlled (Open, or Draft when `is_draft` is sent), `number` is generated when omitted, and the submitted `staff_id` assigns staff member(s) rather than changing the creator. The same operation is also reachable via `POST /work_orders/{id}`.

client_id.description: Identifier of the client this work order belongs to. The client must not be suspended.

number.description: Work order number. Auto-generated when left empty.

delivery_date.description: Expected delivery / finish date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be on or after the start date.

budget.description: Budget amount for this work order.

budget_currency.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget.

staff_id.description: Staff member to assign to this work order. Does not change the recorded creator.

is_draft.description: Set to `1` to save the work order as a Draft with relaxed validation. Defaults to `0`.

message.description: Set for the closed-work-order precondition (e.g. "Work Order is closed, you can't edit"); `null` on validation failures, where the detail is in `validation_errors`.

validation_errors.description: Field name → reason. Present when validation fails.

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a work order by its identifier.

Requires permission to edit/remove the work order, and the work order must have no blocking related transactions (invoices, credit notes, refunds, expenses, requisitions, purchase orders, etc.) — otherwise the request is rejected with `403`. Its start date must not fall within a closed financial period.

For API callers the deletion is confirmed automatically (no confirmation step). On success the deleted-confirmation message is returned with HTTP 200.

message.description: Returned when the caller lacks permission or the work order has blocking related transactions.

get.description: Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of work-order appointments (follow-up appointments attached to work orders). Supports filtering by work order, partner, action, status and appointment id. Requires permission to view appointments/notes. Requires the Work Orders plugin to be enabled.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of items per page (1–1000, default 20).

parameters.name: item_id
parameters.description: Filter by the related work order id (matches `item_id` or `partner_id`).

parameters.name: work_order_id
parameters.description: Filter by work order id (Work Orders plugin).

parameters.name: partner_id
parameters.description: Filter by the linked partner (client) id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Filter by a specific appointment id.

parameters.name: status_id
parameters.description: Filter by status (0 Scheduled, 1 Done, 2 Dismissed). Defaults to `0` (Scheduled) when omitted.

200.description: A paginated list of work-order appointments.

item_type.description:
Type of record the appointment is attached to. For work-order appointments this is always `8`.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Client |
| 2 | Invoice |
| 3 | Estimate |
| 4 | Purchase order |
| 5 | Staff |
| 6 | Supplier |
| 7 | Product |
| 8 | Work order |
| 9 | Appointment |
| 10 | Shift |
| 11 | Booking |

item_id.description: Id of the related work order.

staff_id.description: Id of the staff member who created the appointment. `0` means the account owner.

status.description:
Appointment status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Scheduled |
| 1 | Done |
| 2 | Dismissed |

recurring_appointment_id.description: Id of the recurring series this appointment belongs to, if any.

partner_id.description: Id of the linked partner (the work order's client).

share_with_partner.description: Whether the appointment is shared with the linked partner.

403.description: The caller lacks permission for this operation.

post.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a work-order appointment (a follow-up appointment attached to a work order). The appointment fields are wrapped in a `WorkOrderAppointment` object; `item_id` (the work order id) and `date` are required. Optionally include a `RecurringAppointment` object (with `recurring` set to `1`) to create a repeating appointment. Requires permission to add appointments/notes. Returns `202` with the new appointment's `id`. Requires the Work Orders plugin to be enabled.

item_id.description: The work order id to attach the appointment to. **Required.**

date.description: Appointment start date/time. **Required.** Must be earlier than `end_date`.

end_date.description: Appointment end date/time. Optional; computed from `duration` when omitted.

duration.description: Appointment length in hours (numeric) or as `HH:MM`. Optional; defaults to 1 hour and is used to compute `end_date` when `end_date` is not supplied.

staff_id.description: Id of the creating staff member, or an array of staff ids to assign. Defaults to the authenticated staff when omitted.

status.description: On creation the status is set to `0` (Scheduled) automatically.

recurring.description: Set to `1` to create a repeating appointment; supply the recurrence in the `RecurringAppointment` object.

share_with_partner.description: Share the appointment with the linked partner (the work order's client).

period_unit.description: Repeat interval (number of `unit_name` units between occurrences).

400.description: Validation failed; `validation_errors` lists the offending fields.

403.description: The caller lacks permission for this operation.

404.description: The referenced work order does not exist.
